## 固定收益開場論點

8月26日美國固定收益市場溫和走弱，跌勢由實質殖利率上升帶動，讓聯準會仍保有升息選項，但長端未重回先前的失序狀態。2年期、5年期與10年期美國公債殖利率均上升2個基點，分別至4.19%、4.37%與4.66%；30年期則上升1個基點至5.18%。2s10s殖利率曲線維持在47個基點，2s30s趨平1個基點至99個基點。這波近乎平行的變動值得注意：盤勢沒有再現財政因素驅動的陡峭化，活動數據轉弱與油價下跌也未能延續前一交易日存續期間交易的漲勢。

通膨組成透露的緊縮信號，比名目殖利率的小幅變動更強。10年期實質殖利率上升2個基點至2.34%，完全解釋10年期名目殖利率的升幅；10年期損益兩平通膨率則維持在2.32%。7月核心PCE月增0.2%、年增3.3%，兩者均符合預期，整體物價指數仍較一年前高出3.7%。實質消費支出持平。這批數據削弱立即升息的理由，卻未出現足以完全排除升息的連續通膨降溫證據；利率市場估計9月升息機率為43%，並已完全反映12月前升息25個基點。

能源帶來較明確的短期通膨降溫動能，卻未能壓低殖利率。伊朗與阿曼從臨時航運框架推進至涵蓋荷姆茲海峽的收益分配協議後，布蘭特原油下跌2.31%至$86.53，WTI下跌0.63%至$81.84。美國殖利率走高之際，美元指數上升0.21%；這種跨資產反應更符合利率路徑重新定價，而非財政疑慮再度引發資金撤離。儘管美元回升，黃金仍上漲0.85%至$4,677.70，顯示替代性價值儲存工具的需求未退。股票與廣泛信用工具近乎持平：S&P 500下跌0.02%，LQD下跌0.07%，主要高收益債基金約下跌0.02%。收盤走勢沒有顯示風險偏好全面退潮。

因此，市場主線是通膨黏性約束下的聯準會有條件按兵不動，而非長端紓壓交易全面回歸。房市與服務業數據疲弱，顯示高利率正傳導至需求；但通膨水準仍高、部分經濟活動仍具韌性，使這些數據無法主導政策反應函數。美國財政部更積極的債務管理，已提高放空長債的成本並抑制殖利率曲線陡峭化，但30年期殖利率收盤仍高於5%。與此同時，歐洲與日本出現支持各自升息循環的新理由，大型企業借款人擴大尋找資金來源，多檔困境債務則更接近透過法律程序分配損失。美國利率變動不大，基準殖利率曲線之外的固定收益影響卻不小。

## 通膨黏性遇上需求轉弱

7月PCE同時讓聯準會辯論的兩方都有理由堅持立場。核心物價月增0.2%，幅度溫和且符合預期，但年增率3.3%仍遠高於2%目標。整體物價年增3.7%，更凸顯物價水準問題。扣除能源與住房的服務通膨上升0.3%，其中投資組合管理與投資顧問服務價格上漲5.6%，為一年來最大增幅。近期通膨數據小幅上修，也減弱最新單月數據帶來的寬慰。報告未顯示通膨全面重新加速，但也未證明通膨正穩定回到目標。

需求細項讓短期按兵不動更有依據。經通膨調整後的消費支出，在5月與6月強勁增長後維持不變。核心商品支出下降0.8%，實質服務支出則受交通、餐飲與住宿帶動上升0.3%。部分商品支出疲弱可能是因Amazon把Prime Day促銷從7月提前至6月，因此單月降幅誇大了購買力實際減弱的程度。實質可支配所得上升0.4%，為1月以來最大增幅，儲蓄率升至4個月高點3%。家庭一方面放慢支出，一方面重建所得與儲蓄，反映消費降溫，而非突然中斷。

房市釋出更明確的利率敏感訊號。7月新屋銷售年率從修正後的67.8萬戶下降10.5%至60.7萬戶，低於市場共識的62萬戶。儘管新建住宅在房市成交中占比異常偏高，高房貸利率、營建成本與不確定性仍使建商信心疲弱。新屋價格中位數已降至5年低點，建商也持續提供優惠，但簽約量仍降至6個月低點。成交量疲弱顯示，價格讓利已無法完全抵銷融資成本。這證實既有緊縮政策正傳導至需求，卻不足以證明通膨黏性已經消失。

地區商業數據進一步印證這種分化。里奇蒙聯準銀行製造業指數8月從5降至4，低於市場共識的7，但出貨指數從8改善至11；服務業營收則從-3惡化至-8。因此，該地區製造業產出仍在擴張，較廣泛的服務業卻轉弱。結合實質消費持平與房市受挫，這些數據不支持9月急於升息；但核心通膨3.3%且製造業出貨維持正值，也讓官員有理由保留緊縮傾向。

市場反應正好反映這種平衡。2年期殖利率升至4.19%，但仍比一個月前低14個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升、通膨補償不變，顯示投資人當日要求更高的實質報酬，而非上調中期通膨定價。美元走強傳達相同訊息：PCE報告強到足以恢復部分利率對美元的支撐，卻不足以引發廣泛風險資產賣壓。聯準會主席Kevin Warsh現在必須說明，需要累積多少通膨證據，才會從有條件按兵不動轉為再次升息。週三收盤反映的是市場對這道門檻的不確定性，而非9月結果已成定局。

## 油價紓壓與更廣泛的通膨壓力

荷姆茲海峽外交進展已明顯超越先前的臨時框架。伊斯蘭革命衛隊發言人Hossein Mohebbi表示，伊朗與阿曼已就雙方在海峽水域與收益的分配達成協議。油價連續第三個交易日下跌，布蘭特原油跌2.31%，減輕近期整體通膨的部分壓力。不過，實際營運仍有限制：伊朗警告，與阿曼達成協議不代表水道會立即重新開放，已公布的收益條款也未證實航運量恢復。收盤走勢肯定外交進展，卻未把實體運輸正常化視為已經完成。

歐洲較持久的能源風險，如今集中在天然氣而非原油。天然氣價格接近5個月高點，冬季合約價格超過一年前的2倍，庫存僅達63%，為2009年以來同期最低。天然氣占歐盟能源結構21%，在英國則約占25%至35%。不同於原油，經荷姆茲海峽運輸的LNG沒有替代航線，可吸收長期短缺的戰略庫存也很有限。因此，原油下跌僅在邊際上改善全球通膨動能，歐洲國內電力、工業與家庭成本管道仍暴露於風險。

歐洲央行（ECB）執委Isabel Schnabel把這項風險轉化為明確的政策主張。她表示，現行政策利率不太可能在中期內使通膨回到目標，且在能源壓力傳導至薪資前，有必要進一步緊縮。她的論點也以需求為基礎：歐元區產出在停滯後於第2季成長0.4%，德國成長率獲上修，而財政政策、國防支出與AI熱潮均支撐經濟活動。歐元區7月通膨已達2.9%，市場幾乎完全反映升息25個基點、使存款利率升至2.5%。Schnabel的警告並非只著眼於油價；需求具韌性，提高天然氣與其他供給成本透過二輪效應延續的風險。

日本則提供另一輪緊縮循環的獨立證據。7月企業服務價格較一年前上升3.6%，為5月以來最快增幅，此前3個月數據均獲上修。航線拉長推升成本，海運服務價格因而暴增67.4%，創1986年開始統計以來最大增幅。較早數據也有顯著修正：4月初值為上升3%，目前已上修至3.6%。這種修正型態使目前的加速更難被忽視，也不排除7月數據日後再上修。市場估計日本央行在9月18日會議升息的機率約為80%，副總裁Ryozo Himino即將發表的談話，將是判斷官員是否認同市場定價的下一項指標。

泰國顯示，同一項全球衝擊未必導致相同的政策反應。泰國央行連續第三次會議一致決議，將隔夜附買回利率維持在1%，並形容政策立場寬鬆。第2季經濟僅成長1.9%，在東南亞6個主要經濟體中最慢；即使大型企業放款改善，中小企業信用仍然緊縮。官員預期受聖嬰現象影響，通膨將一路上升至2027年第1季，之後回到低檔，但目前既不適合升息，也不適合再度降息。央行保留在危機中寬鬆的空間，同時警告進一步降息對實體經濟的傳導可能不佳。第2季已實現的核准投資案支出為2,550億泰銖，其中AI相關投資超過1,270億泰銖，說明整體投資強勁可以與國內信用條件不均並存。

巴西則更接近另一端的政策循環。8月上旬通膨降至4.24%，低於4.33%的預測中位數，並回到3%目標上下1.5個百分點的容忍區間內。物價月減0.4%，降幅大於預估的0.32%，主因一次性電費抵減使住房成本下降1.41%，機票降價也帶動交通價格下降1%。交換利率整條曲線下滑，2027年1月合約最多下跌2.6個基點。部分改善屬於暫時性，加上選舉相關社會支出支撐需求，因此仍須審慎解讀其組成。即便如此，在連續第四次降息25個基點、使Selic利率降至14%後，這份報告給予央行更多政策空間。

各國政策路徑正因同類衝擊的傳導方式不同而分化。歐洲與日本面臨進口能源與運費上升，同時需求仍足以讓央行考慮升息。泰國著重保護疲弱且不均衡的復甦，巴西則在政策利率極高之際，回應已實現的通膨下降。美國介於兩者之間：原油下跌與實質支出持平支持耐心等待，但核心通膨高於目標且所得背景具韌性，使再次升息仍有可能。因此，傑克森霍爾年會登場時，全球帶有緊縮傾向，卻沒有共同時間表。

## 官方資產負債表重新引導存續期間

美國財政部積極調整債務管理，對相對價值交易的影響，遠比對美國借款絕對成本的影響更明顯。Morgan Stanley Investment Management的Vishal Khanduja，在財政部承諾至少把流通中10年期至30年期債券的買回規模提高1倍後，減碼5s30s陡峭化部位。自消息公布以來，5s30s殖利率差已收窄約10個基點；Barclays估計，增購規模每年可能達$640億，約相當於目前20年期與30年期供給的15%。Citadel Securities策略師Frank Flight也撤回7月的看空判斷，理由是通膨證據改善及放空部位過度擁擠。這些都是投資人行為的當前變化：官方需求提高後，忽略長端殖利率下行風險的代價也隨之上升。

8月26日收盤也顯示技術面支撐的極限。儘管油價下跌、消費轉弱，30年期殖利率仍上升1個基點至5.18%，10年期亦升至4.66%。財政部必須以現金或新發債券支應買回，無法創造準備金。因此，焦點正轉向11月4日的季度再融資。Deutsche Bank、Morgan Stanley與Citigroup策略師正在評估多種可能，包括轉向國庫券與較短天期公債、維持或縮減長債標售、擴大買回操作，以及在極端情境下，最終取消交易狀況欠佳的20年期公債。Bessent已排除在該次再融資前調整定期標售。目前尚未發生任何改變，而把發債轉向前端，只會轉移存續期間與再融資風險，不會減少總借款。

法國顯示，期限管理無法取代財政共識。法國10年期公債殖利率近20年來首度升破4%，相對德國公債的溢價達86個基點，略低於2012年以來最寬收盤水準。債務約占GDP的117%，政府已懷疑能否把今年財政赤字從2025年的5.1%降至5%。總理Sebastien Lecornu計畫在9月底提出的預算案中，不增稅而尋求結構性節省，但這項作法面臨反對黨與企業團體阻力。若國會未能在4月18日與5月2日的總統大選投票前通過預算，緊急融資法案可能使赤字至少增加GDP的0.5個百分點。Fitch的審查將揭開評等行事曆序幕，而法國是否進入另一輪降評階段，將取決於財政執行情況，而非表面目標。

捷克則明確作出相反的政治選擇。國會推翻總統Petr Pavel的否決，放寬財政限制，以允許創紀錄的基礎建設支出。舊規則原將2027年中央政府赤字上限設為1,500億捷克克朗；官員目前預期赤字將高於今年的3,100億，但低於4,000億捷克克朗。整體赤字預估占GDP的2.8%，仍低於歐盟3%的上限，公共債務占GDP約46%，也仍是歐盟最低之列。這樣的起始條件讓布拉格比巴黎擁有更多空間，但預期借款需求增加已推高債券殖利率。反對黨提出的違憲挑戰，也為包含創紀錄零售債發行的融資計畫增添執行風險。

中國轉向隔夜基準，是官方資產負債表傳導的另一種形式。招商銀行正籌備最多人民幣20億元、與DR001隔夜附買回利率連結的3年期浮動利率債券，將是中國本地商業銀行首度發行此類債券。中國進出口銀行已於8月稍早採用該基準，銀行也開始將其用於放款。中國人民銀行正把操作目標從7天期附買回利率轉向隔夜天期，並增加隔夜流動性操作。資產與負債端採用相同參考利率，可改善貨幣政策傳導，並在銀行利差接近歷史低點之際保護獲利，讓央行有更大寬鬆彈性。這項變化屬於市場基礎設施調整，而非對中國債券存續期間方向的即時判斷，但會改變政策流動性傳導至債券與貸款定價的方式。

印尼央行準總裁則回應另一種制度溢價。Destry Damayanti向國會表示，與政府協調不會削弱印尼央行的獨立性，並將維持具前瞻性的預防式政策利率操作。她作出保證的背景，包括總裁Perry Warjiyo提前離任、總統Prabowo Subianto的姪子獲任命為副總裁，以及央行職權擴及成長與就業。印尼盾近乎持平，10年期政府公債殖利率維持3個基點升幅，顯示這番聲明防止疑慮再度升高，卻未將其消除。她提議的任期為2026年至2031年，因此當政府8%的成長目標帶來壓力時，公信力將取決於匯市干預、流動性供給及減少高殖利率SRBI券種的作法，是否仍與物價穩定一致。

墨西哥主權債定價也呈現官方安撫與現券市場之間的類似落差。5年期CDS為80個基點，低於總統Claudia Sheinbaum於2024年10月就任時的120個基點，政府並以利差收窄作為市場信心的證據。美元債卻傳達較不樂觀的訊息：Bank of America估計，墨西哥債券利差比同評等國家寬39個基點，相當於正式評等低約1.5個級距。對Pemex長達8年的支持合計$1,300億；相關援助使該石油公司的債務從2016年高峰占GDP的9.3%降至4%，卻也把風險轉向主權。墨西哥仍維持投資等級，但Moody's於5月將其降至最低投資等級，S&P也把展望列為負向。多個拉丁美洲主權CDS下降，仍無法消除墨西哥相對偏高的財政風險溢價。

## AI融資擴大尋求買方基礎

SoftBank可能進行的離岸發債，已把AI融資從普遍的供給疑慮，轉化為明確的個別發行人事件。該公司正討論發行$100億至$200億的美元與歐元計價債券，時間最快可能在9月，用以償還投資OpenAI所動用的$400億過橋貸款一部分，並支應其他AI投資承諾。SoftBank預定在10月前向OpenAI投資接近$650億。若發行規模達區間上緣，這將成為今年亞洲發行人規模最大的離岸交易，並大幅縮減估計超過$200億的資金缺口。

信用市場隨即要求規模與不確定性的風險補償。SoftBank票息8.5%的美元債下跌2.3美分至約98，創該債券4月發行以來最大單日跌幅；5年期CDS利差擴大10.7個基點，為一個多月來最大增幅。公司表示正考慮多種再融資方案，發行金額尚未決定。這項保留說法代表執行方式、幣別組合與期限都仍未確定，但次級市場反應已明確指出疑慮所在：把過橋融資轉為較長天期債務，是把集中的AI投資承諾轉移給規模大得多的公開市場債權人。

規劃中的144A格式將是SoftBank逾10年來首次採用，並會讓美國機構投資人參與交易。擴大銷售對象相當重要，因為公司同時規劃在日本發行創紀錄的1兆日圓零售債券，並已取得以OpenAI持股擔保的$100億保證金貸款。這項保證金融資含有可能要求補繳現金擔保品或提前還款的契約條款，因此不能視為毫無摩擦的永久資本。SoftBank在4月也發行了$36億美元與歐元債券，其中包括10年期、票息8.5%的債券。離岸機構、日本家庭與擔保貸款機構，都被要求為同一投資計畫的不同層級提供資金。

這項個別發行人事件，位於更廣泛的資本競爭之中。美國企業今年已為資料中心及相關AI投資發行超過$4,100億債券。韓國正籌備至少1,350兆韓元、即$9,750億的晶片與資料中心企業投資；Citigroup預期，在已協助客戶募得約$600億後，韓國企業2026年的國際債券與股票發行將創紀錄。這些計畫處於不同階段，不應合併視為已確定的借款。不過，這些計畫顯示融資需求已從美國超大規模雲端業者，延伸至亞洲科技龍頭與投資控股公司。

SoftBank的價格反應才是關鍵的邊際訊號。大型借款人可以分散幣別、發行格式與投資人基礎，但目前若要取得資金，就必須為槓桿、結構性支持與變現不確定性提供足夠補償。即使信用風險集中於個別發行人，超大型交易仍可能與主權債爭奪存續期間資金，因為投資人都是以同一批有限資產負債表支應投資。週三廣泛信用債基金近乎持平，並不與這項結論矛盾。市場仍有選擇性，而非已經關閉：整體高收益債風險維持穩定，但再融資需求異常龐大的特定借款人遭到劇烈重新定價。

## 債權人優先順位進入落實階段

Brightline與Assured Guaranty達成協議，使這宗市政債市場規模最大的潛在重整案之一，更接近聲請美國《破產法》第11章。若這家佛州鐵路公司提出聲請，相關安排將提供至少$3.5億新貸款，時間可能在數週內。Brightline負債達$55億，多數債務以困境價格交易。協議尚未生效，公司仍可尋求其他庭內或庭外方案，但已承諾的債務人持有資產融資（DIP融資），讓Assured有機會取得較高優先順位，並對重整程序發揮更大影響力。

現有資本結構說明各方爭奪的原因。Invesco、Nuveen與First Eagle持有Brightline優先順位最高的$22億債務，其中約$11億由Assured提供保證，任何變更均須獲其同意。由Redwood Capital、Aristeia Capital與Nut Tree Capital領導的避險基金團體，持有$11億公司債的多數部位，其順位低於市政債。另有約$20億債務由順位更低的市政債組成。破產融資通常優先於既有債權，因此誰控制新資金融資，就會同時影響重整程序與回收路徑。這項協議提高急迫性，卻未決定最終企業價值或債權人分配。

Altice International的擔保債權人也試圖藉訴訟爭取優先順位。Arini Capital Management、Silver Point、King Street、Sona、Diameter與Invesco已組成聯盟，Elliott也正洽談加入；若加入，該團體將占擔保債務約60%。成員準備提起訴訟，並爭取優於委員會外債權人的待遇。其主張聚焦於50億歐元、即$53億的集團內貸款，以及把葡萄牙與多明尼加共和國業務移出受限制集團，涉嫌違反契約條款。Altice Financing表示，債權人未證明具備所需持有部位或授權，因此違約通知無效；債權人則駁斥這項抗辯。目前的核心爭議不再只是Patrick Drahi電信集團的槓桿，而是資產移轉與是否參與委員會，會不會改變同一擔保債權類別內的回收。

Braskem的庭外程序顯示，各券種獲得的支持極不平均。代表224億巴西里拉、即$43億且占受影響債務39.6%的債權人，支持這項$110億重整案，略高於啟動程序所需的三分之一門檻。公司現在有90天，爭取過半債權支持以取得法院核准；申請時仍有60.4%尚未加入。主要股東Petrobras與IG4 Capital，或經核准的第三方，預計提供新股本或承諾補足缺口，但金額、結構與時程仍未解決。

各系列參與率顯示談判籌碼所在。2081年到期次順位債券約有67%加入；2028年到期、票息4.5%的債券約有60%加入；2033年到期、票息7.25%與2031年到期、票息8.5%的債券也各約有58%加入。2050年到期、票息5.875%的債券參與率降至約30%，2041年到期、票息7.125%的債券則約13%；規模最大的2030年到期、票息4.5%債券，支持與反對幾乎各半。銀行要求增加擔保品，但公司未接受。程序已跨過第一道法律門檻，不過參與率分散顯示，任何足以約束債權人的方案，仍須協調差異極大的期限、順位與回收誘因。

儘管廣泛風險工具幾乎沒有波動，這些案件各自仍具重大影響。Brightline正透過潛在的超優先順位融資分配控制權，Altice債權人爭議平等待遇與資產流失，Braskem則必須從參與率差異懸殊的各債券系列中湊足法定多數。基準殖利率影響每一項估值，但各信用標的下一步價格變化，目前主要由法律地位主導。整體市場平靜，可以與困境資本結構內回收權利快速重新分配同時存在。

## 後續市場意涵

Warsh在8月28日傑克森霍爾年會的演說，將決定8月26日實質殖利率上升只是小幅數據調整，還是更明確緊縮路徑的起點。關鍵在於他如何看待核心PCE年增3.3%、實質消費持平與整體物價年增3.7%，以及他為9月升息設定哪些條件。若政策反應函數能在需求降溫時容許通膨逐步下降，將支持按兵不動並限制前端殖利率上行。若更重視通膨水準、數據修正或全球供給壓力，市場已完全反映的12月升息就更可能提前，並由2年期至5年期區段率先調整。

能源下一階段取決於實體航運，而非另一則外交頭條。船隻是否實際通過荷姆茲海峽、伊朗與阿曼收益安排能否持續、歐洲天然氣庫存與運費走勢，將顯示布蘭特原油下跌能否擴大為持久的通膨紓壓。若水道重開且庫存上升，歐洲與日本利率路徑以及美國損益兩平通膨率的壓力都將降低。若LNG限制持續，或黑海穀物運輸再次受阻，即使原油維持在近期高點以下，進口通膨壓力仍會廣泛存在，迫使央行區分油價下跌與供給衝擊真正減弱。

後續融資事件將揭示，官方與民間資產負債表能否重新引導供給，而不推高整體經濟的市場出清殖利率。美國財政部11月再融資必須說明，擴大買回將由國庫券、較短天期公債、現金或長債標售調整中的何者支應；SoftBank的最終規模、幣別、期限、144A結構與定價，將測試機構投資人承接AI槓桿的能力；Brightline、Altice與Braskem則必須把債權人聯盟轉化為可執行的優先順位與新資金條款。若執行順利，可抑制特定產業的波動。若財政部前端供給負擔更重、SoftBank定價大幅走寬，或重整案未獲多數債權人支持，就表示改變期限、發行市場或法律順位，只是重新分配風險，並未減少最終必須由市場吸收的資金總量。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 26 U.S. fixed-income close was a modest real-yield selloff that kept the Federal Reserve's tightening option alive without restoring the long end's earlier disorder. The 2-year, 5-year and 10-year Treasury yields each rose 2 basis points, to 4.19%, 4.37% and 4.66%, while the 30-year added 1 basis point to 5.18%. The 2s10s curve held at 47 basis points and 2s30s flattened 1 basis point to 99 basis points. That near-parallel move matters: the session did not produce another fiscal steepening impulse, but neither did softer activity and lower oil generate a follow-through rally after the previous day's duration gains.

The inflation composition was more restrictive than the small nominal move suggests. The 10-year real yield rose 2 basis points to 2.34%, accounting for the full increase in the nominal 10-year yield, as the 10-year breakeven remained at 2.32%. Core PCE increased 0.2% in July and 3.3% from a year earlier, both in line with expectations, while the broader price index was still 3.7% above its year-earlier level. Real consumer spending was flat. The data weakened the case for an immediate hike without supplying the repeated disinflation needed to close the option altogether; rate markets put the probability of a September increase at 43% and fully priced a quarter-point move by December.

Energy offered a clearer near-term disinflation impulse but failed to pull yields down. Brent fell 2.31% to $86.53 after Iran and Oman advanced from an interim shipping framework to a revenue-sharing agreement covering the Strait of Hormuz, and WTI declined 0.63% to $81.84. The Dollar Index rose 0.21% as U.S. yields moved higher, a cross-asset response more consistent with rate-path repricing than renewed fiscal flight. Gold nevertheless gained 0.85% to $4,677.70, preserving demand for an alternative store of value even as the dollar recovered. Equities and broad credit vehicles were nearly unchanged: the S&P 500 slipped 0.02%, LQD fell 0.07%, and the main high-yield funds lost about 0.02%. Nothing in that close indicated a generalized withdrawal of risk appetite.

The hierarchy is therefore a conditional Fed hold constrained by sticky inflation, rather than a clean return to the long-end relief trade. Weak housing and services evidence showed that high rates are reaching demand, yet the inflation level and firmer pockets of activity prevented those releases from dominating the reaction function. Treasury's more activist debt management has changed the cost of being short long bonds and contained curve steepening, but the close still left the 30-year above 5%. At the same time, Europe and Japan supplied fresh reasons for their own tightening cycles, large corporate borrowers widened the search for capital, and several distressed credits moved closer to legal loss allocation. The U.S. rates move was small; the fixed-income consequences outside the benchmark curve were not.

## Sticky Inflation Meets Softer Demand

July PCE gave both sides of the Federal Reserve debate enough evidence to resist capitulation. A 0.2% monthly increase in core prices was moderate and matched expectations, yet the 3.3% annual rate remained well above the 2% objective. The broader 3.7% annual reading made the level problem more visible. Services inflation excluding energy and housing rose 0.3%, including a 5.6% increase in portfolio-management and investment-advice prices, the largest in a year. Small upward revisions to recent inflation readings also limited the reassurance available from the latest month. The release did not show renewed acceleration across the board, but it did not establish a reliable return to target.

Demand details made a near-term hold more defensible. Inflation-adjusted consumer spending was unchanged after strong gains in May and June. Core-goods outlays fell 0.8%, whereas real services spending rose 0.3% on transportation, restaurants and accommodation. Some of the goods weakness may reflect Amazon moving its Prime Day promotion into June from July, so the monthly decline overstates the underlying loss of purchasing power. Real disposable income rose 0.4%, the strongest increase since January, and the saving rate climbed to a four-month high of 3%. Households slowed spending while rebuilding income and savings, a combination that points to cooling rather than a sudden break in consumption.

Housing supplied the sharper rates-sensitive signal. July new-home sales fell 10.5% to a 607,000 annual rate from a revised 678,000 and missed the 620,000 consensus. High mortgage rates, construction costs and uncertainty have kept builder confidence weak even though new construction has carried an unusually large share of housing turnover. Median new-home prices have fallen to a five-year low and builders continue to use incentives, but contract signings still reached a six-month low. That weak volume says price concessions are no longer fully offsetting financing costs. It is relevant to the policy transmission already in place, not sufficient evidence that inflation persistence has disappeared.

Regional business data reinforced the split. The Richmond Fed manufacturing index eased to 4 in August from 5 and fell short of the 7 consensus, but its shipments index improved to 11 from 8. Services revenues deteriorated to -8 from -3. Manufacturing output was therefore still expanding in the district even as the broader service side weakened. Taken with flat real consumption and the housing setback, the mix argues against urgency for September. Taken with 3.3% core inflation and positive manufacturing shipments, it also leaves officials with a reason to preserve a tightening bias.

The market response captured that balance. Two-year yields rose to 4.19%, but remained 14 basis points below their level one month earlier. The 10-year real yield increased while inflation compensation was unchanged, showing that investors demanded more real return rather than marking up medium-term inflation on the day. The stronger dollar carried the same message: the PCE report was firm enough to restore some rate support to the currency, though not strong enough to produce a broad risk selloff. Chair Kevin Warsh now has to explain how much cumulative inflation evidence is needed to convert a conditional hold into another increase. Wednesday's close priced uncertainty about that threshold, not a settled September outcome.

## Oil Relief Meets a Broader Inflation Front

The Strait of Hormuz diplomacy delivered a material advance beyond the prior interim framework. Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said Iran and Oman had agreed on their respective shares of the strait's waters and revenues. Oil fell for a third session, and Brent's 2.31% decline took some pressure out of the immediate headline-inflation channel. The qualification is operational: Iran has cautioned that an agreement with Oman does not imply an immediate reopening of the waterway, and the announced revenue terms did not establish resumed shipping volumes. The close rewarded diplomatic progress without treating physical normalization as complete.

Europe's more persistent energy risk now sits in natural gas rather than crude. Gas prices were near five-month highs, winter contracts cost more than twice their year-earlier level, and storage was only 63% full, the lowest for the time of year since 2009. Gas accounts for 21% of the European Union's energy mix and roughly 25% to 35% of the United Kingdom's. Unlike oil, LNG moving through Hormuz has no alternative shipping route and few strategic stockpiles can absorb an extended shortfall. Falling crude therefore improves the global inflation impulse at the margin while leaving Europe's domestic power, industrial and household-cost channel exposed.

ECB Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel translated that exposure into an explicit policy preference. She said the current policy rate was unlikely to return inflation to target over the medium term and that further tightening was necessary before energy pressure reached wages. Her argument also rested on demand: euro-area output grew 0.4% in Q2 after stagnating, German growth was revised higher, and she identified fiscal policy, defense spending and the AI boom as supports to activity. July euro-area inflation had reached 2.9%, and markets were close to fully pricing a 25-basis-point increase that would take the deposit rate to 2.5%. Schnabel's warning is not simply an oil call. Resilient demand raises the risk that gas and other supply costs persist through second-round effects.

Japan supplied independent evidence for another tightening cycle. Corporate service prices rose 3.6% from a year earlier in July, the fastest pace since May after the previous three months were revised higher. Ocean-freight service prices surged 67.4%, the largest increase in a series extending back to 1986, as longer shipping routes raised costs. Earlier readings have been revised materially: April's initial 3% increase now stands at 3.6%. That revision pattern makes the current acceleration harder to dismiss and leaves open the possibility that July will also be marked higher. Markets assigned about an 80% probability to a Bank of Japan increase at the September 18 meeting, with Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino's coming remarks the next indication of whether officials accept that pricing.

Thailand demonstrated why the same global shock need not produce the same policy response. The Bank of Thailand unanimously kept its one-day repo rate at 1% for a third meeting and described policy as accommodative. Q2 growth was only 1.9%, the slowest among the six major Southeast Asian economies, and credit remained tight for small and medium-sized companies even as lending to large corporates improved. Officials expect inflation to rise through Q1 2027 because of El Nino before returning to low levels, but see neither a hike nor another cut as appropriate now. The bank retained room to ease in a crisis while warning that additional reductions may transmit poorly into the real economy. AI-linked investment accounted for more than 127 billion baht of the 255 billion baht in approved-project spending realized in Q2, illustrating why aggregate investment strength can coexist with uneven domestic credit conditions.

Brazil moved closer to the other side of the cycle. Early-August inflation slowed to 4.24%, below the 4.33% median forecast and inside the 3% target's 1.5-percentage-point tolerance band. Prices fell 0.4% on the month against a -0.32% estimate, led by a one-time electricity credit that cut housing costs 1.41% and cheaper airfares that helped transportation prices fall 1%. Swap rates declined across the curve, with the January 2027 contract down as much as 2.6 basis points. The composition argues for caution because part of the improvement is temporary and election-related social spending supports demand. Even so, the release gives the central bank more latitude after its fourth consecutive quarter-point reduction took the Selic rate to 14%.

These policy paths are diverging around the transmission of the same shocks. Europe and Japan face imported energy and freight costs alongside sufficient demand to consider higher rates. Thailand is protecting a weak and uneven recovery, and Brazil is responding to a realized decline in inflation from a very high policy setting. The U.S. sits between them: falling crude and flat real spending support patience, but above-target core inflation and a resilient income backdrop keep another increase plausible. Jackson Hole therefore arrives with a global tightening bias but no common timetable.

## Official Balance Sheets Redirect Duration

Treasury activism is changing relative-value behavior more decisively than it is changing the absolute cost of U.S. borrowing. Vishal Khanduja of Morgan Stanley Investment Management reduced a 5s30s steepener after Treasury committed to at least double purchases of outstanding 10- to 30-year debt. The 5s30s gap had narrowed about 10 basis points since the announcement, and Barclays estimated the increase could amount to $64 billion annually, equivalent to roughly 15% of current 20- and 30-year supply. Citadel Securities strategist Frank Flight separately reversed his July bearish call, citing improved inflation evidence and crowded short positioning. These are current changes in investor behavior: official demand has made long-end downside in yields more expensive to ignore.

The August 26 close also marked the limit of that technical. The 30-year yield still rose 1 basis point to 5.18%, and the 10-year increased to 4.66% despite lower oil and softer consumption. Treasury must fund buybacks with cash or new issuance; it cannot create reserves. Attention is consequently moving to the November 4 quarterly refunding. Strategists at Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley and Citigroup are considering a shift toward bills and shorter notes, steady or smaller long-bond auctions, larger buyback operations, and, in a tail scenario, eventual elimination of the poorly trading 20-year maturity. Bessent has ruled out changes to regular auctions before that refunding. No shift has yet occurred, and moving issuance toward the front end transfers duration and rollover risk rather than reducing total borrowing.

France shows why maturity management cannot substitute for fiscal agreement. Its 10-year yield moved above 4% for the first time in nearly two decades and the premium over Germany reached 86 basis points, just short of its widest closing level since 2012. Debt is around 117% of GDP, and the government already doubts it can reduce this year's deficit to 5% from 5.1% in 2025. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu plans to seek structural savings without new taxes in a budget due in late September, an approach that faces resistance from opposition parties and business groups. If parliament fails to approve a budget before the April 18 and May 2 presidential votes, emergency funding legislation could add at least 0.5 percentage point of GDP to the deficit. Fitch's review begins the ratings calendar, with fiscal execution rather than the headline target determining whether France enters another downgrade phase.

The Czech Republic made the opposite political choice explicit. Lawmakers overrode President Petr Pavel's veto and loosened fiscal limits to permit record infrastructure spending. The old rule would have capped the 2027 central-government deficit at 150 billion koruna; officials now expect a shortfall above this year's 310 billion but below 400 billion koruna. The broader deficit is projected at 2.8% of GDP, still below the European Union's 3% ceiling, and public debt near 46% of GDP remains among the bloc's lowest. That starting position gives Prague more room than Paris, but bond yields have already risen with expected borrowing needs. A constitutional challenge from opposition parties adds execution risk to a funding program that also includes record retail issuance.

China's shift toward an overnight benchmark is a different form of official balance-sheet transmission. China Merchants Bank is preparing as much as 2 billion yuan of 3-year floating-rate notes linked to the DR001 overnight repo rate, the first such issue by a local commercial lender. The Export-Import Bank of China used the benchmark earlier in August, and banks have begun applying it to loans as well. The PBOC has been moving its operational target from the 7-day repo rate toward the overnight tenor and adding overnight liquidity operations. Using the same reference across assets and liabilities can improve monetary transmission and protect bank margins near record lows, giving the central bank more flexibility to ease. The change is market infrastructure rather than an immediate direction call on Chinese duration, but it alters how policy liquidity reaches bond and loan pricing.

Indonesia's prospective central-bank governor addressed a separate institutional premium. Destry Damayanti told parliament that coordination with the government would not dilute Bank Indonesia's independence and retained a preemptive, forward-looking approach to the policy rate. The reassurance follows the early departure of Governor Perry Warjiyo, the appointment of President Prabowo Subianto's nephew as a deputy governor and an expanded mandate covering growth and employment. The rupiah was little changed and the 10-year government yield retained a 3-basis-point increase, suggesting the statement prevented renewed concern without removing it. Her proposed term runs from 2026 to 2031, so credibility will depend on whether currency intervention, liquidity provision and the move away from high-yield SRBI securities remain consistent with price stability when the government's 8% growth ambition creates pressure.

Mexico's sovereign pricing supplied an analogous gap between official reassurance and the cash bond market. Five-year CDS stood at 80 basis points, down from 120 when President Claudia Sheinbaum took office in October 2024, and the government cited that compression as evidence of confidence. Dollar bonds told a less comfortable story: Bank of America estimated Mexico traded 39 basis points wider than similarly rated countries, equivalent to about 1.5 rating notches below its formal standing. Eight years of support for Pemex totaled $130 billion; that assistance reduced the oil company's debt to 4% of GDP from a 9.3% peak in 2016, but transferred risk toward the sovereign. Mexico remains investment grade, yet Moody's cut it to the lowest investment-grade tier in May and S&P placed the outlook at negative. Falling CDS across several Latin American sovereigns does not resolve that relative fiscal penalty.

## AI Funding Reaches for a Larger Buyer Base

SoftBank's potential offshore sale moved AI financing from a general supply concern into a defined issuer event. The company is discussing a $10 billion to $20 billion offering in dollars and euros, possibly as early as September, to repay part of a $40 billion bridge loan used for its OpenAI investment and to finance other AI commitments. SoftBank is scheduled to invest close to $65 billion in OpenAI by October. At the upper end, the bond would be the largest offshore transaction by an Asian issuer this year and would materially reduce a funding gap estimated above $20 billion.

Credit markets immediately charged for the scale and uncertainty. SoftBank's 8.5% dollar bond fell 2.3 cents to about 98, its largest daily decline since the note was issued in April, and 5-year CDS widened 10.7 basis points, the biggest increase in more than a month. The company said it was considering several refinancing options and had not decided the amount. That caveat leaves execution, currency mix and maturity open, but the secondary response already identifies the concern: converting a bridge facility into term debt transfers a concentrated AI commitment into a much larger public creditor base.

The contemplated 144A format would be SoftBank's first in more than a decade and would open the transaction to U.S. institutional investors. That broader distribution is important because the company is simultaneously planning a record ¥1 trillion retail bond in Japan and has secured a $10 billion margin loan backed by its OpenAI stake. The margin facility includes covenants that can require cash collateral or early repayment, so it cannot be treated as frictionless permanent capital. SoftBank also sold $3.6 billion in dollar and euro bonds in April, including the 10-year 8.5% note. Offshore institutions, Japanese households and secured lenders are all being asked to fund different layers of the same investment program.

The issuer-specific event sits inside a broader competition for capital. U.S. companies had already sold more than $410 billion of bonds this year for data centers and related AI investment. Korea is preparing at least 1,350 trillion won, or $975 billion, of corporate investment in chips and data centers, and Citigroup expects record international debt and equity issuance by Korean companies in 2026 after helping clients raise about $60 billion so far. Those plans are at different stages and should not be aggregated as settled borrowing. They show, however, that the financing demand extends from U.S. hyperscalers to Asian technology champions and investment holding companies.

SoftBank's price response is the relevant marginal signal. Large borrowers can diversify currency, format and investor base, but access now requires enough compensation for leverage, structural support and uncertain monetization. An oversized transaction can also compete with sovereign duration even if its credit risk is idiosyncratic, because investors fund it from the same finite balance sheets. Wednesday's nearly unchanged broad credit funds do not contradict that conclusion. The market was selective rather than closed: aggregate high-yield risk held steady while a named borrower with an unusually large refinancing need repriced sharply.

## Creditor Priority Moves Toward Implementation

Brightline's agreement with Assured Guaranty moved one of the municipal market's largest prospective restructurings closer to Chapter 11. The arrangement would provide the Florida railroad with at least $350 million of new loans if it files, potentially within weeks. Brightline has $5.5 billion of obligations and much of its debt trades at distressed prices. The agreement is not yet effective, and the company can pursue another in-court or out-of-court structure, but a committed debtor-in-possession facility gives Assured a route to senior priority and greater influence over the restructuring process.

The existing capital structure explains the contest. Invesco, Nuveen and First Eagle hold Brightline's $2.2 billion of highest-priority debt, of which Assured guarantees about $1.1 billion and must consent to changes. A hedge-fund group led by Redwood Capital, Aristeia Capital and Nut Tree Capital holds a majority of $1.1 billion in corporate notes junior to the municipal debt. Roughly $2 billion of additional obligations consists of lower-ranking municipal bonds. Bankruptcy financing normally ranks ahead of existing claims, so control of the new-money facility affects both the process and the path to recovery. The agreement increases urgency without determining final enterprise value or creditor distributions.

Altice International's secured creditors are also trying to convert litigation effort into priority. Arini Capital Management, Silver Point, King Street, Sona, Diameter and Invesco formed a bloc, with Elliott in discussions to join; its addition would take the group to roughly 60% of secured debt. Members are prepared to litigate and seek preferential treatment over creditors outside the committee. Their claim centers on alleged covenant breaches involving EUR5 billion, or $5.3 billion, of intercompany loans and the transfer of the Portugal and Dominican Republic businesses outside the restricted group. Altice Financing says the default notice is invalid because the creditors did not establish the required holdings or authority, and creditors reject that defense. The live issue is no longer only leverage at Patrick Drahi's telecom group, but whether asset transfers and committee participation change recoveries within the same secured class.

Braskem's out-of-court process revealed how unevenly support is distributed across instruments. Creditors representing 22.4 billion reais, or $4.3 billion and 39.6% of affected debt, backed the $11 billion restructuring, just above the one-third threshold needed to begin. The company now has 90 days to win support from more than half of claims for court approval; 60.4% had not adhered at filing. Main shareholders Petrobras and IG4 Capital, or approved third parties, are expected to provide or backstop fresh equity, but amount, structure and timing remain unresolved.

Series-level participation locates negotiating leverage. About 67% of subordinated notes due 2081 joined, as did roughly 60% of the 4.5% notes due 2028 and about 58% of both the 7.25% 2033 and 8.5% 2031 bonds. Participation fell to around 30% for the 5.875% 2050 notes and about 13% for the 7.125% 2041 issue; the largest series, the 4.5% 2030 notes, was almost evenly divided. Banks sought additional collateral that the company did not accept. The process has cleared its first legal threshold, but the dispersion shows that a plan capable of binding creditors still has to reconcile very different maturity, ranking and recovery incentives.

These cases are independently material even though broad risk vehicles barely moved. Brightline is allocating control through prospective super-senior financing, Altice creditors are disputing equal treatment and asset leakage, and Braskem must assemble a statutory majority from bond series with sharply different participation. Benchmark yields affect every valuation, but legal position now dominates the next price step in each credit. Broad market calm can coexist with rapid redistribution of recovery rights inside distressed capital structures.

## Forward Market Significance

Warsh's August 28 Jackson Hole address now determines whether the August 26 real-yield increase remains a small data adjustment or becomes the start of a clearer tightening path. The relevant combination is his treatment of 3.3% core PCE, flat real consumption and a 3.7% headline price level, together with the conditions he assigns to a September move. A reaction function that tolerates gradual disinflation while demand cools supports a hold and limits front-end upside. Greater weight on the inflation level, revisions or global supply pressure makes the fully priced December increase more likely to move forward, with the 2- to 5-year sector carrying the first adjustment.

Energy's next phase depends on physical shipping rather than another diplomatic headline. Actual vessel transit through Hormuz, the durability of the Iran-Oman revenue arrangement, European gas storage and freight costs will show whether Brent's decline can broaden into a persistent inflation relief. Reopening with rising storage would reduce pressure on European and Japanese rate paths as well as U.S. breakevens. Continued LNG constraints or renewed Black Sea grain disruption would keep imported inflation broad even if crude remains below its recent peak, forcing central banks to distinguish lower oil from a genuinely weaker supply shock.

The next funding events will reveal whether official and private balance sheets can redirect supply without raising the economy-wide clearing yield. Treasury's November refunding must specify whether larger buybacks are financed by bills, shorter notes, cash or changes to long-bond auctions; SoftBank's final size, currency, maturity, 144A structure and pricing will test institutional capacity for AI leverage; and Brightline, Altice and Braskem must convert creditor blocs into enforceable priority and fresh-money terms. Smooth execution can contain sector-specific volatility. A larger front-end Treasury burden, a sharply wider SoftBank print or failed restructuring majorities would show that changing maturity, venue or legal rank redistributes risk without reducing the amount of capital that ultimately has to be absorbed.
